Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $n\ge2$ and let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a bounded connected open set with smooth boundary. Write $H^1(\Omega)=W^{1,2}(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ and let $H_0^1(\Omega)$ be the $H^1$-closure of $C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R)$. Define the boundary trace-data space $\mathcal B_\Omega:=H^1(\Omega)/H_0^1(\Omega)$ with quotient norm; the trace-quotient lemma identifies this quotient with the fixed-atlas $H^{1/2}(\partial\Omega)$ boundary data convention of the scalar conductivity map. Let $\gamma\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega;\operatorname{Sym}_n(\mathbb R))$ be uniformly positive definite, so some $0<c\le C<\infty$ satisfy $c|\xi|^2\le \xi^T\gamma(x)\xi\le C|\xi|^2$ for all $x\in\overline\Omega$ and $\xi\in\mathbb R^n$. For $f=[U]\in\mathcal B_\Omega$, a weak solution with boundary datum $f$ is a class $u_{\gamma,f}\in H^1(\Omega)$ with $[u_{\gamma,f}]=f$ and

$$\int_\Omega \gamma\nabla u_{\gamma,f}\cdot\nabla\varphi\,dx=0\qquad(\varphi\in H_0^1(\Omega)).$$

The weak anisotropic Dirichlet-to-Neumann map is the bilinear-form candidate $\Lambda_\gamma:\mathcal B_\Omega\times\mathcal B_\Omega\to\mathbb R$ given, whenever the weak solution exists, by

$$\langle\Lambda_\gamma f,h\rangle:=\int_\Omega\gamma\nabla u_{\gamma,f}\cdot\nabla V_h\,dx,$$

where $V_h\in H^1(\Omega)$ is any representative of $h$. The local anisotropic conductivity well-posedness lemma proves existence and uniqueness for every boundary class, independence of the representative $V_h$, and boundedness on $\mathcal B_\Omega\times\mathcal B_\Omega$; it therefore makes this candidate a bounded bilinear map. The map is the boundary energy form for the equation $\operatorname{div}(\gamma\nabla u)=0$. Under the trace-quotient isomorphism and the local boundedness result, this form gives the usual weak map into the dual $H^{-1/2}(\partial\Omega)$ with the scalar convention.

there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

$\{0,\ldots,k\}$, and it contains the zero multi-index.

The real and complex $L^p$ classes use the conventions in

$u\in L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ such that, for every $\alpha\in\mathcal A_k$,
there is an $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ class with a locally integrable
representative $v_\alpha$ satisfying
$$\int_\Omega u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,dx =(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int_\Omega v_\alpha\varphi\,dx \qquad\text{for every }\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega).$$
Here the weak derivative is the one in
Weak derivative of a locally integrable function. Under
The Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), local integrability of $L^p$ representatives and
invariance under null-set changes follow from

Uniqueness of a weak derivative as an almost-everywhere class gives uniqueness of each

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, let $k\in\mathbb N_0$, let $1\le p\le\infty$, and let
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$.

Every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ belongs to
$W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. Indeed $\varphi$ is bounded with compact support,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ for every exponent in range, and each of
its classical partial derivatives is again smooth and compactly supported,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and is the corresponding weak derivative
by [[lem-classical-derivatives-are-weak-derivatives]].

Define the **zero-boundary Sobolev space**
$$W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K):=\overline{C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)},$$
the closure taken in the normed space
$(W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K),\|\cdot\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)})$ of
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]. The norm is a genuine norm on classes
by [[lem-sobolev-norm-is-well-defined-and-definite]], so this is the usual
metric closure of a subset of a normed space: $u\in W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$
if and only if for every $\delta>0$ there is
$\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with
$\|u-\varphi\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}<\delta$. Write
$H_0^k(\Omega):=W_0^{k,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ when the scalar field is fixed by
context.

Three warnings are part of the definition. First, this is a closure of
almost-everywhere classes, and all its equalities are equalities of Sobolev
classes. Second, no pointwise boundary values and no trace characterization
are asserted: a description of $W_0^{k,p}$ by vanishing boundary data belongs
to the later trace theory and is not used here. Third, the closure is defined
for every $1\le p\le\infty$, but for $p=\infty$ it is not claimed that every
compactly supported $W^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$ function lies in $W_0^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$;
the definition merely names the closure of the test functions.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a real or complex Hilbert space, let $a$ be a bounded coercive sesquilinear form on $H$ with constants $M,\alpha$ ([[def-bounded-coercive-and-symmetric-sesquilinear-forms]]), and let $F:H\to\mathbb K$ be a bounded conjugate-linear functional with norm $\|F\|=\sup_{\|v\|\le1}|F(v)|$. The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume the Axiom of Choice, hence Countable Choice. Let $n\ge2$, let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a bounded connected domain with smooth boundary, and let $\gamma\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega;\operatorname{Sym}_n(\mathbb R))$ be uniformly positive definite. Let $F:\overline\Omega\to\overline\Omega$ be a diffeomorphism smooth through the boundary, with smooth inverse and $F|_{\partial\Omega}=\operatorname{id}$. For $x=F(y)$, put $J_F(y)=|\det DF(y)|$ and define

$$ (F_*\gamma)(x)=\frac{DF(y)\,\gamma(y)\,DF(y)^T}{J_F(y)},\qquad y=F^{-1}(x). $$

Then $F_*\gamma$ is a smooth uniformly positive-definite matrix conductivity and its weak anisotropic Dirichlet-to-Neumann map equals that of $\gamma$. Explicitly, for every pair of boundary trace-data classes $f,h\in\mathcal B_\Omega:=H^1(\Omega)/H_0^1(\Omega)$,

$$\langle\Lambda_{F_*\gamma}f,h\rangle=\langle\Lambda_\gamma f,h\rangle,$$

where each map is the weak energy form $\langle\Lambda_\gamma f,h\rangle=\int_\Omega\gamma\nabla u_{\gamma,f}\cdot\nabla V_h\,dx$, $u_{\gamma,f}$ is the unique weak solution with boundary class $f$, and $V_h$ is any $H^1$ representative of $h$.

The same gauge invariance has a Riemannian form. Let $M$ be a compact smooth manifold with boundary, $g$ a smooth Riemannian metric, $\Gamma\subseteq\partial M$ relatively open, and $\Phi:M\to M$ a smooth diffeomorphism with $\Phi|_\Gamma=\operatorname{id}$. Define $(\Phi^*g)_p(v,w):=g_{\Phi(p)}(D\Phi_pv,D\Phi_pw)$. The cotangent inner product $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_g$ is induced by $g^{-1}$, and in coordinates $dV_g=\sqrt{\det(g_{ij})}|dx^1\cdots dx^n|$. A smooth function $u$ is $g$-harmonic when $\int_M\langle du,d\psi\rangle_g\,dV_g=0$ for every $\psi\in C_c^\infty(M^\circ)$. Then $u\circ\Phi$ is $\Phi^*g$-harmonic; for any two smooth $g$-harmonic functions $u,v$,

$$\int_M\langle d(u\circ\Phi),d(v\circ\Phi)\rangle_{\Phi^*g}\,dV_{\Phi^*g}=\int_M\langle du,dv\rangle_g\,dV_g.$$

If the boundary traces of $u,v$ are supported in $\Gamma$, then composition by $\Phi$ leaves both traces fixed, so the local energy measurement of every such smooth harmonic pair is unchanged. In particular, if for each $f\in C_c^\infty(\Gamma)$ the Dirichlet solutions for $g$ and $\Phi^*g$ with trace $f$ are unique and smooth, then the corresponding local energy DN maps agree.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $n\ge2$ and let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a bounded connected open set with smooth boundary. Write $H^1(\Omega)=W^{1,2}(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ and let $H_0^1(\Omega)$ be the $H^1$-closure of $C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R)$. Define the boundary trace-data space $\mathcal B_\Omega:=H^1(\Omega)/H_0^1(\Omega)$ with quotient norm; the trace-quotient lemma identifies this quotient with the fixed-atlas $H^{1/2}(\partial\Omega)$ boundary data convention of the scalar conductivity map. Let $\gamma\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega;\operatorname{Sym}_n(\mathbb R))$ be uniformly positive definite, so some $0<c\le C<\infty$ satisfy $c|\xi|^2\le \xi^T\gamma(x)\xi\le C|\xi|^2$ for all $x\in\overline\Omega$ and $\xi\in\mathbb R^n$. For $f=[U]\in\mathcal B_\Omega$, a weak solution with boundary datum $f$ is a class $u_{\gamma,f}\in H^1(\Omega)$ with $[u_{\gamma,f}]=f$ and

$$\int_\Omega \gamma\nabla u_{\gamma,f}\cdot\nabla\varphi\,dx=0\qquad(\varphi\in H_0^1(\Omega)).$$

The weak anisotropic Dirichlet-to-Neumann map is the bilinear-form candidate $\Lambda_\gamma:\mathcal B_\Omega\times\mathcal B_\Omega\to\mathbb R$ given, whenever the weak solution exists, by

$$\langle\Lambda_\gamma f,h\rangle:=\int_\Omega\gamma\nabla u_{\gamma,f}\cdot\nabla V_h\,dx,$$

where $V_h\in H^1(\Omega)$ is any representative of $h$. The local anisotropic conductivity well-posedness lemma proves existence and uniqueness for every boundary class, independence of the representative $V_h$, and boundedness on $\mathcal B_\Omega\times\mathcal B_\Omega$; it therefore makes this candidate a bounded bilinear map. The map is the boundary energy form for the equation $\operatorname{div}(\gamma\nabla u)=0$. Under the trace-quotient isomorphism and the local boundedness result, this form gives the usual weak map into the dual $H^{-1/2}(\partial\Omega)$ with the scalar convention.

derivations.claim: Write $R_\varepsilon(r)=r(1+\varepsilon(1-r^2))$ for $0\le r\le1$. Then $R_\varepsilon(0)=0$, $R_\varepsilon(1)=1$, and $R_\varepsilon'(r)=1+\varepsilon-3\varepsilon r^2\ge1-2\varepsilon>0$. Thus $R_\varepsilon$ is a strictly increasing bijection of $[0,1]$ to itself; $F_\varepsilon$ preserves each radial ray, is bijective on the ball, and fixes the boundary pointwise.

At the origin $DF_\varepsilon(0)=(1+\varepsilon)I_n$ and $J_{F_\varepsilon}(0)=(1+\varepsilon)^n>0$. At $r>0$ the radial derivative is $R_\varepsilon'(r)>0$ and each tangential eigenvalue is $R_\varepsilon(r)/r=1+\varepsilon(1-r^2)>0$. By continuity, $R_\varepsilon'$ stays positive on $[0,1+\delta]$ for some $\delta>0$. The same radial formula extends $F_\varepsilon$ to a smooth diffeomorphism from the ball of radius $1+\delta$ onto its image, which contains a neighborhood of $\overline{B^n}$; its inverse is smooth there. Thus the inverse is smooth through the boundary and the differential is nonsingular on the closed ball.

Since $F_\varepsilon(0)=0$, the pushforward formula in [F1] gives $\widetilde\gamma_\varepsilon(0)=DF_\varepsilon(0)DF_\varepsilon(0)^T/J_{F_\varepsilon}(0)=(1+\varepsilon)^{2-n}I_n$. Because $n\ge3$ and $\varepsilon>0$, this differs from $I_n$, so the pushed-forward conductivity is nontrivial.

The hypotheses of [F1] hold for $\gamma=I_n$ and $F_\varepsilon$, so $\Lambda_{\widetilde\gamma_\varepsilon}=\Lambda_{I_n}$. The example therefore exhibits a distinct smooth anisotropic conductivity with exactly the same boundary energy map, caused by the stated boundary-fixing change of variables.

$\mathbb R^{d}$, $d\ge1$, which is bi-Lipschitz and whose derivatives in both directions are bounded,
then for every measurable $u:V'\to\mathbb K$,
$$\|u\circ\Psi\|_{W^{s,p}(V)}\le C(\Psi,s,p)\,\|u\|_{W^{s,p}(V')}$$
and symmetrically with $\Psi^{-1}$; in particular the Slobodeckij norm
$\|\cdot\|_{W^{s,p}}$ of [[def-fractional-slobodeckij-space-on-euclidean-space]]
is preserved up to equivalence by such coordinate changes. Here the norm on an open set uses the same double integral restricted to that set, with its $L^p$ term. Bounded derivatives alone on arbitrary open sets do not imply the bi-Lipschitz hypothesis.

(ii) Consequently two finite boundary chart families with subordinate
partitions, as in
[[def-fractional-sobolev-space-on-a-compact-c-one-boundary]], define
equivalent norms on $\partial\Omega$: the sum norms differ by multiplicative
constants depending only on the two atlases, the dimension and $s,p$, so
$W^{s,p}(\partial\Omega)$ is well defined as a set and its topology is
atlas-independent.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $k\ge1$, $1\le p\le\infty$ and
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. Let $U,V\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open
and let $\Phi:U\to V$ be a $C^k$ diffeomorphism with inverse
$\Psi:=\Phi^{-1}:V\to U$. Fix open sets $U_0\subset\subset U$ and
$V_0\subset\subset V$ with $\Phi(U_0)\subseteq V_0$, and suppose that on
$\overline{U_0}$ the derivatives of $\Phi$ through order $k$ are bounded and
that on $\overline{V_0}$ the derivatives of $\Psi$ through order $k$ are
bounded; in the situation of
[[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]] these are exactly the compact
patches on which the flattening chart and its inverse have bounded derivatives
through order $k$. Then:

1. for every $u\in W^{k,p}(V_0;\mathbb K)$ the composition
$u\circ\Phi$ belongs to $W^{k,p}(U_0;\mathbb K)$, and for every
$1\le|\alpha|\le k$ its weak derivatives satisfy, almost everywhere on
$U_0$,
$$D^\alpha(u\circ\Phi)=\sum_{1\le|\beta|\le|\alpha|}\bigl((D^\beta u)\circ\Phi\bigr)\,P_{\alpha\beta}\bigl(D\Phi,\dots,D^k\Phi\bigr),$$
where $P_{\alpha\beta}$ is a universal polynomial with integer coefficients,
whose values on $\overline{U_0}$ are bounded by a constant depending only on
$n,k$ and the stated bounds for $\Phi$;

2. there is a constant $C$, depending only on $n$, $k$, $p$ and the two sets of
chart bounds, with
$$\|u\circ\Phi\|_{W^{k,p}(U_0)}\le C\,\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(V_0)}\qquad\text{for all }u\in W^{k,p}(V_0;\mathbb K).$$
If in addition $\Psi(V_0)\subseteq U_0$ (equivalently, under the stated
$\Phi(U_0)\subseteq V_0$, $\Phi(U_0)=V_0$), the same assertion holds for
composition with $\Psi$ from $W^{k,p}(U_0)$ to $W^{k,p}(V_0)$.

For $k=1$ only the first derivatives of $\Phi$ and $\Psi$ enter, so bounded
$C^1$ chart and inverse data suffice; no $C^1$-only claim is made for $k>1$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, let $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, and let
$\eta\in C^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and
$u\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. For
$\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^n$, suppose that for every $\gamma\le\alpha$ there is
$v_\gamma\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with
$D^\gamma u=v_\gamma$ weakly. Then $\eta u$ has a weak $\alpha$-derivative,
and its almost-everywhere class is
$$D^\alpha(\eta u)=\sum_{\beta\le\alpha}\binom{\alpha}{\beta}(D^\beta\eta)D^{\alpha-\beta}u\quad\text{in }L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\mathbb K).$$
where $D^\beta\eta$ is the classical derivative and products are pointwise
products of representatives. The resulting class does not depend on the
representatives.

For $k\in\mathbb N_0$ and $1\le p\le\infty$, if
$u\in W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and $D^\beta\eta\in L^\infty(\Omega)$ for
every $|\beta|\le k$, then $\eta u\in W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and the same
formula holds in $L^p$ for every $|\alpha|\le k$. In particular,
$\eta\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ is a sufficient condition on the
multiplier for this global conclusion.

For $\Omega=\varnothing$ all classes are zero and the identity holds. The
pairing convention is bilinear, with no complex conjugation.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k\ge1$, $1\le p<\infty$,
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, and let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a
bounded $C^k$ domain in the graph sense of
[[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]. Then the set of restrictions
to $\Omega$ of functions in $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb K)$ is dense in
$W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$: for every $u\in W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and
every $\delta>0$ there is $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb K)$ with
$\|\varphi|_\Omega-u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}<\delta$.

The exponent range is $1\le p<\infty$; the result asserts no density in the
$W^{k,\infty}$ norm, and it does not hold on arbitrary open sets, as the
companion examples page shows.

Assume the Axiom of Choice, used to invoke the published real and complex
$L^p$ completeness results through their Countable-Choice interface. Let
$\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, $n\ge1$, let $k\in\mathbb N_0$,
$1\le p\le\infty$, and $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. Then
$W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$, equipped with the displayed norm of
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], is a complete normed space over
$\mathbb K$.

Both endpoints $p=1$ and $p=\infty$ are included, as is $k=0$, where the
assertion reduces to the completeness of $L^p$. If $\Omega=\varnothing$, then
$W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ is the zero space and the assertion is trivial.
The Axiom of Choice is used only to derive Countable Choice for the two
published completeness interfaces; no other selection is made. Representative
selection inside the finitely many coordinate classes is finite and
choice-free.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $d\ge1$, $1<p<\infty$, $\theta=1-1/p$,
$H=\mathbb R^d\times(0,\infty)$, and let $T_+$ be the half-space trace of
[[thm-trace-estimate-on-the-half-space]]. Write
$|Du|^p:=\sum_{j=1}^{d+1}|D_ju|^p$ for the sum of the $p$-th powers of the
weak first derivatives, and $[\cdot]_{\theta,p}$ for the Slobodeckij seminorm
of [[def-fractional-slobodeckij-space-on-euclidean-space]]. Then for every
$u\in W^{1,p}(H;\mathbb K)$ with $g=T_+u$,
$$[g]_{\theta,p}^p\le C(d,p)\int_H|Du|^p\,dx=C(d,p)\sum_{j=1}^{d+1}\|D_ju\|_{L^p(H)}^p\le C(d,p)\|u\|_{W^{1,p}(H)}^p;$$
equivalently $T_+:W^{1,p}(H;\mathbb K)\to W^{\theta,p}(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb K)$
is a bounded operator.

The homogeneous estimate is scale invariant: for $r>0$ and
$u_r(x',t):=u(rx',rt)$ one has $g_{u_r}(x')=g(rx')$ and
$$[g_{u_r}]_{\theta,p}^p=r^{-d+p\theta}[g]_{\theta,p}^p,\qquad \int_H|Du_r|^p\,dx=r^{-d+p\theta}\int_H|Du|^p\,dx,$$
because $p\theta=p-1$; so both sides of the homogeneous estimate scale with
the same exponent $r^{-d+p\theta}$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, be a
bounded $C^1$ domain in the graph sense of
[[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]], let $\partial\Omega$ carry the
chart-independent surface measure of
[[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]] and
[[lem-surface-integral-is-independent-of-c-one-boundary-charts]], let
$1\le p<\infty$ and $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. Then there is a
unique bounded linear operator
$$T:W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)\longrightarrow L^p(\partial\Omega;\mathbb K)$$
with $Tu=u|_{\partial\Omega}$ for every
$u\in C(\overline\Omega)\cap W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$, and it satisfies
$\|Tu\|_{L^p(\partial\Omega)}\le C(\Omega,p)\|u\|_{W^{1,p}(\Omega)}$. On each
boundary chart the operator is the flat half-space trace of
[[thm-trace-estimate-on-the-half-space]] transported by the flattening
diffeomorphism, and the chartwise definitions agree on overlaps; uniqueness
holds because two bounded operators agreeing on the dense subspace
$C(\overline\Omega)\cap W^{1,p}(\Omega)$ are equal.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, be a
bounded $C^1$ domain and $1\le p<\infty$. Then the kernel of the trace
operator of [[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]] equals the
zero-boundary Sobolev space:
$$\{u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K):Tu=0\}=W_0^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K),$$
the $W^{1,p}$-closure of $C_c^\infty(\Omega)$
([[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]]).

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, let $k\in\mathbb N_0$, let $1\le p\le\infty$, and let
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$.

Every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ belongs to
$W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. Indeed $\varphi$ is bounded with compact support,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ for every exponent in range, and each of
its classical partial derivatives is again smooth and compactly supported,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and is the corresponding weak derivative
by [[lem-classical-derivatives-are-weak-derivatives]].

Define the **zero-boundary Sobolev space**
$$W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K):=\overline{C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)},$$
the closure taken in the normed space
$(W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K),\|\cdot\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)})$ of
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]. The norm is a genuine norm on classes
by [[lem-sobolev-norm-is-well-defined-and-definite]], so this is the usual
metric closure of a subset of a normed space: $u\in W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$
if and only if for every $\delta>0$ there is
$\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with
$\|u-\varphi\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}<\delta$. Write
$H_0^k(\Omega):=W_0^{k,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ when the scalar field is fixed by
context.

Three warnings are part of the definition. First, this is a closure of
almost-everywhere classes, and all its equalities are equalities of Sobolev
classes. Second, no pointwise boundary values and no trace characterization
are asserted: a description of $W_0^{k,p}$ by vanishing boundary data belongs
to the later trace theory and is not used here. Third, the closure is defined
for every $1\le p\le\infty$, but for $p=\infty$ it is not claimed that every
compactly supported $W^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$ function lies in $W_0^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$;
the definition merely names the closure of the test functions.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, be a
bounded $C^1$ domain, $1<p<\infty$, $\theta=1-1/p$, and let $T$ be the trace
operator of [[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]]. Then there is
a bounded linear operator
$$R:W^{\theta,p}(\partial\Omega;\mathbb K)\longrightarrow W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$$
with $T\circ R=\mathrm{id}_{W^{\theta,p}(\partial\Omega)}$ and
$\|Rg\|_{W^{1,p}(\Omega)}\le C(\Omega,p)\|g\|_{W^{\theta,p}(\partial\Omega)}$.
Moreover, for every open neighbourhood $U$ of $\partial\Omega$ in
$\mathbb R^n$ there is such an operator $R_U$ whose image is contained in the
classes vanishing a.e. outside $U$, with
$\|R_Ug\|_{W^{1,p}(\Omega)}\le C(\Omega,p,U)\|g\|_{W^{\theta,p}(\partial\Omega)}$.
The right inverse is not unique and no canonical choice is claimed.

derivations.claim: On the common smooth core, the identity between the fixed-atlas and Euclidean $W^{1,2}$ norms is bounded in both directions. Indeed, each fixed chart representative is obtained by multiplying by a fixed smooth cutoff and composing with a smooth flattening chart, so [F3] bounds the finite fixed-atlas sum by the Euclidean norm. Conversely, the finite partition of unity writes $u$ as the sum of its localized chart pieces; pull each piece back and use [F3] to bound the Euclidean $W^{1,2}$ norm by the fixed-atlas sum. The constants are finite because the atlas and partition are finite. By the density and completeness in [F3], the identity extends to bounded inverse maps on the completions. Since the two norms are equivalent on $C_c^\infty(\Omega)$, their closures give the same zero-boundary subspace.

For $u\in H^1_{\rm fix}$, take its localized boundary-chart representatives in the fixed-atlas definition. Apply [F4] to each representative (reflecting $t<0$ to $t>0$ when required), and sum the finitely many resulting local traces. The fixed-atlas norm [F1] gives a bounded map $T:H^1_{\rm fix}\to H^{1/2}_{\rm fix}$. For smooth $u$ this sum is the classical boundary restriction because the partition equals one near the boundary and the half-space traces agree with classical restriction. As an $L^2$-valued map, this trace agrees with the Euclidean trace [F5]: the maps are bounded into $L^2$ by [F2] and [F5], and the Euclidean and fixed $H^1$ norms are equivalent by step 1.1, so equality on the dense smooth core extends to all of $H^1$.

If $Tu=0$ in $H^{1/2}_{\rm fix}$, it is zero as an $L^2$ class by [F2]; the $L^2$ trace agreement of step 2.1 and [F6] imply $u\in H^1_{0,\rm E}$. Step 1.1 identifies this with $H^1_{0,\rm fix}$. Conversely, if $u\in H^1_{0,\rm fix}$, approximate it in the fixed $H^1$ norm by interior compactly supported smooth functions. Each has zero classical trace, so continuity of $T$ gives $Tu=0$. Therefore $\ker T=H^1_{0,\rm fix}$.

By [F7] and the boundary-norm equivalence [F2], the Euclidean $L^2$ trace has a bounded right inverse $R:H^{1/2}_{\rm fix}(\partial\Omega)\to H^1_{\rm E}(\Omega)$. The norm equivalence of step 1.1 makes $R$ bounded into $H^1_{\rm fix}$ as well. For every boundary class $f$, the Euclidean trace of $Rf$ is $f$; by step 2.1 the fixed trace agrees with it in $L^2$, hence as an $H^{1/2}_{\rm fix}$ class. So $T$ is onto. The kernel identity of step 3.1 induces a bounded bijection $\bar T:H^1_{\rm fix}/H^1_{0,\rm fix}\to H^{1/2}_{\rm fix}$. For any representative $u+v$ with $v\in H^1_{0,\rm fix}$, step 2.1 gives $\|Tu\|_{H^{1/2}}\le C\|u+v\|_{H^1_{\rm fix}}$; taking the infimum shows $\bar T$ is bounded. Also $\|\bar T^{-1}f\|\le\|Rf\|_{H^1_{\rm fix}}\le C_R\|f\|_{H^{1/2}}$, so its inverse is bounded. Composing with the quotient identity isomorphism of step 1.1 proves the asserted Euclidean quotient identification.
